title: Event binding
summary: React to clicks with (click) and call a method that changes the component's data.

quiz.q: Which syntax runs `save()` when a button is clicked?
quiz.explain: Parentheses bind to an event: `(click)="save()"`. Square brackets are for properties, and plain `onclick` is not how Angular listens.

quiz.q: Finish the method so it adds one to `votes`.
quiz.explain: Inside a class method, `this` is the component. `this.votes` is the property.

options: The event object the browser created
The previous value of the input
quiz.explain: `$event` carries details about what happened, for example the DOM event with `target.value` for typed text.

quiz.q: Click the line that has a mistake. The click should call the method.
quiz.explain: `vote` without parentheses only names the method. Write `(click)="vote()"` to call it.

exercise.task:
Finish `vote.component.ts`.

- The first button uses `(click)="vote()"` and the second uses `(click)="reset()"`.
- `vote()` adds one to `this.votes`.
- `reset()` sets `this.votes` back to `0`.
hints: Each button needs an event binding, and the class needs the two methods.
Inside a method use `this.votes`. For adding one you can write `this.votes++`.

checks.name: The class has votes starting at 0
